objectives: To understand the fundamental concepts of relational database management systems.
To design database schemas using Entity-Relationship modeling and normalization techniques.
To formulate complex database queries using Structured Query Language (SQL) and relational algebra.
To examine transaction processing, concurrency control protocols, and database recovery mechanisms.
To introduce NoSQL architectures and modern storage paradigms.

course_outcomes.description: Apply relational algebra and relational calculus to formulate declarative database queries.
Design conceptual schema using Entity-Relationship diagrams and map them to relational schemas.
Construct optimized SQL queries including joins, subqueries, views, and aggregate functions.
Evaluate relational schemas using 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF functional dependency decomposition to eliminate anomalies.
Analyze ACID transaction properties, serializability, lock-based concurrency control, and write-ahead logging recovery.

units.title: Introduction & Database System Architecture
units.topics: Data models, schemas, and instances; Three-schema architecture and data independence; Database languages and interfaces; Database users and administrators; Entity-Relationship model: entities, attributes, entity sets, relationships, constraints, weak entity sets, Extended ER features (specialization, generalization, categorization).

units.title: Relational Data Model & Relational Algebra
units.topics: Relational model concepts, relational integrity constraints; Relational algebra operations: Selection, Projection, Union, Set Difference, Cartesian Product, Rename, Natural Join, Outer Joins, Division; Tuple Relational Calculus and Domain Relational Calculus; Overview of QBE.

units.title: SQL & Query Processing
units.topics: Data Definition Language (DDL) commands: CREATE, ALTER, DROP; Data Manipulation Language (DML) commands: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; Advanced SELECT queries: nested subqueries, correlated subqueries, set operations, aggregate functions, GROUP BY, HAVING; Integrity constraints, assertions, triggers, views; Overview of query optimization and cost estimation.

units.title: Database Design Theory & Normalization
units.topics: Informal design guidelines for relation schemas; Functional dependencies: Armstrong's axioms, closure of functional dependencies, minimal cover; Normal forms based on primary keys: First Normal Form (1NF), Second Normal Form (2NF), Third Normal Form (3NF); Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF); Multi-valued dependencies and Fourth Normal Form (4NF); Lossless join decomposition and dependency preservation.

units.title: Transaction Processing, Concurrency & Recovery
units.topics: Transaction concepts, states, ACID properties; Schedules and serializability: conflict and view serializability; Concurrency control techniques: Two-Phase Locking (2PL), strict 2PL, deadlock prevention and detection, timestamp ordering; Database recovery techniques: deferred update, immediate update, shadow paging, write-ahead logging (WAL), checkpoints.

objectives: To introduce the core services, structures, and system call interfaces of modern operating systems.
To explain process management, threads, multi-programming, and CPU scheduling algorithms.
To study process synchronization mechanisms, critical-section problem solutions, and deadlock handling.
To analyze contiguous and non-contiguous memory management, paging, segmentation, and virtual memory.
To examine file system implementation, directory structures, and secondary storage disk scheduling.

course_outcomes.description: Explain operating system structure, system calls, interrupt handling, and kernel architecture.
Analyze and compare preemptive and non-preemptive CPU scheduling algorithms for responsiveness and throughput.
Implement synchronization primitives (semaphores, mutexes, monitors) to solve classic synchronization problems.
Design and evaluate deadlock prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and detection strategies.
Demonstrate virtual memory techniques including page replacement algorithms (FIFO, LRU, Optimal) and evaluate disk scheduling.

units.title: OS Overview & Process Concept
units.topics: Role and purpose of operating systems, kernel architectures (monolithic, microkernel, hybrid), system calls, OS services; Process concept: process states, Process Control Block (PCB), context switching; Threads: user-level and kernel-level threads, multithreading models; Process scheduling queues, schedulers.

units.title: CPU Scheduling & Process Synchronization
units.topics: Scheduling criteria: CPU utilization, throughput, turnaround time, waiting time, response time; Scheduling algorithms: First-Come First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF), Priority Scheduling, Round Robin (RR), Multilevel Queue Scheduling; Inter-process communication (IPC); Critical Section problem, Peterson's algorithm, hardware synchronization, semaphores, mutex locks, monitors; Classic problems: Producer-Consumer, Readers-Writers, Dining Philosophers.

units.title: Deadlocks
units.topics: Deadlock characterization: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait; Resource allocation graph (RAG); Deadlock prevention strategies; Deadlock avoidance: safe state, Banker's algorithm for single and multiple resource instances; Deadlock detection and recovery.

units.title: Memory Management & Virtual Memory
units.topics: Logical versus physical address space, swapping, contiguous allocation, fragmentation (internal and external), paging, translation lookaside buffer (TLB), multi-level paging, inverted page tables, segmentation; Virtual memory: demand paging, page fault handling, page replacement algorithms (FIFO, Optimal, LRU, LFU, MFU), allocation of frames, thrashing and working set model.

units.title: Storage Management & File Systems
units.topics: File concepts, access methods (sequential, direct, indexed), directory structures, file mounting and protection; File system structure, allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed), free-space management; Secondary storage structure: disk structure, disk scheduling algorithms (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK, C-LOOK), RAID levels.

objectives: To build a solid understanding of layered network architectures (OSI 7-layer and TCP/IP protocol suites).
To study framing, error detection/correction, and medium access control mechanisms.
To master routing algorithms, subnetting, IPv4/IPv6 addressing, and congestion control.
To explore transport protocols (TCP and UDP), flow control, reliability, and socket programming.
To analyze key application layer protocols including DNS, HTTP, SMTP, and network security basics.

course_outcomes.description: Differentiate OSI reference model and TCP/IP protocol stack layers and their respective duties.
Apply error detection (CRC, checksum) and framing algorithms at the Data Link Layer.
Formulate IPv4/IPv6 CIDR subnet masks and evaluate distance-vector and link-state routing protocols.
Contrast TCP and UDP connection semantics, congestion control (AIMD, slow start), and flow control.
Analyze client-server application protocols including DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, DHCP, and SMTP.

units.title: Introduction & Physical / Data Link Layer
units.topics: Network topologies, PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN; Protocol layers: OSI reference model vs TCP/IP protocol suite; Physical layer transmission media; Data link layer design issues: framing, error control, CRC, Hamming codes, flow control: Stop-and-Wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat ARQ; HDLC.

units.title: Medium Access Control (MAC) Sublayer
units.topics: Multiple access protocols: Pure and Slotted ALOHA, CSMA, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA; IEEE 802.3 Ethernet standard, Fast Ethernet, Gigabit Ethernet; IEEE 802.11 Wireless LAN architecture; Bridges, switches, VLANs.

units.title: Network Layer & Routing
units.topics: Network layer design issues, store-and-forward packet switching; Routing algorithms: shortest path routing, Distance Vector Routing (Bellman-Ford), Link State Routing (Dijkstra), hierarchical routing, OSPF, BGP; Congestion control principles; IP addressing: IPv4 classes, CIDR subnetting, NAT, ARP, RARP, ICMP, IPv6 header format and transition strategies.

units.title: Transport Layer
units.topics: Transport service primitives, socket addressing, multiplexing and demultiplexing; User Datagram Protocol (UDP): segment header, checksum; Transmission Control Protocol (TCP): connection establishment (three-way handshake), termination, TCP segment structure, flow control via sliding window, TCP congestion control: slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit, fast recovery.

units.title: Application Layer & Security Fundamentals
units.topics: Domain Name System (DNS): hierarchical namespace, resource records, resolution; Electronic mail: SMTP, POP3, IMAP; HyperText Transfer Protocol (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2), HTTPS, cookies; Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP); Network security introduction: symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, firewalls.

objectives: To explore the phases of a language translator and the construction of lexical analyzers.
To develop top-down and bottom-up parsing techniques for Context-Free Grammars.
To apply syntax-directed translation for intermediate code generation.
To study code optimization algorithms and target machine code generation.

course_outcomes.description: Construct deterministic finite automata and lexical analyzers using regular expressions.
Design LL(1), SLR(1), LR(1), and LALR(1) parsing tables for context-free grammars.
Formulate syntax-directed definitions (SDD) and generate intermediate representations like three-address code.
Apply machine-independent optimizations including loop invariant code motion and common subexpression elimination.
Generate optimized target machine instructions and implement register allocation using graph coloring.

units.title: Introduction to Compilers & Lexical Analysis
units.topics: Phases of a compiler, passes, compiler construction tools; Role of lexical analyzer, tokens, patterns, lexemes; Regular expressions, Thompson's construction to NFA, subset construction to DFA, minimization of DFAs; Lex/Flex tool specification.

units.title: Syntax Analysis (Top-Down & Bottom-Up Parsing)
units.topics: Context-free grammars, derivations, parse trees, ambiguity; Top-down parsing: recursive descent, predictive LL(1) parsing, FIRST and FOLLOW computations; Bottom-up parsing: shift-reduce parsing, operator precedence, LR parsing algorithms (SLR, canonical LR, LALR); Yacc/Bison parser generator.

units.title: Syntax-Directed Translation & Intermediate Code
units.topics: Syntax-directed definitions (SDD), synthesized and inherited attributes, evaluation orders for SDDs; Intermediate representations: syntax trees, postfix notation, three-address code (quadruples, triples, indirect triples); Translation of expressions, type checking, boolean expressions, control flow statements.

units.title: Run-Time Storage & Code Optimization
units.topics: Storage organization, activation records, stack allocation of space, heap management, parameter passing mechanisms; Principles of code optimization: basic blocks, flow graphs, loop optimization, common subexpression elimination, dead code elimination, copy propagation, constant folding.

units.title: Code Generation & Register Allocation
units.topics: Issues in the design of code generators; Target machine description; Simple code generator algorithm; Register allocation and assignment, register allocation by graph coloring; Peephole optimization.

objectives: To introduce fundamental concepts of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.
To study mathematical foundations of regression, classification, and clustering algorithms.
To evaluate model generalization, bias-variance tradeoff, and cross-validation methodologies.
To introduce neural networks, deep learning architectures, and modern ML pipelines.

course_outcomes.description: Formulate supervised learning models including Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, and SVMs.
Analyze decision trees, random forests, and ensemble boosting techniques (AdaBoost, XGBoost).
Apply unsupervised clustering (K-Means, Hierarchical) and dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE).
Evaluate classification performance using precision, recall, F1 score, ROC-AUC, and cross-validation.
Construct multi-layer perceptrons with backpropagation and explain regularizers (L1/L2, dropout).

units.title: Foundations & Supervised Regression
units.topics: Overview of machine learning, types of learning; Linear regression: hypothesis representation, ordinary least squares, gradient descent (batch, stochastic, mini-batch); Polynomial regression; Overfitting, underfitting, bias-variance tradeoff; Regularization: Ridge (L2) and Lasso (L1) regression.

units.title: Supervised Classification Models
units.topics: Logistic regression: sigmoid activation, log-loss cost function, decision boundaries; Naive Bayes classifier, Bayes theorem, Gaussian and Multinomial variants; Support Vector Machines (SVM): maximal margin hyperplane, soft margin, kernel trick (RBF, polynomial kernels); K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN).

units.title: Tree-Based Models & Ensemble Learning
units.topics: Decision tree learning: ID3, C4.5, CART; Splitting criteria: entropy, information gain, Gini impurity; Tree pruning; Ensemble methods: Bagging (Random Forest), Boosting (AdaBoost, Gradient Boost, XGBoost); Stacking and voting classifiers.

units.title: Unsupervised Learning & Dimensionality Reduction
units.topics: Clustering: K-Means algorithm, Elbow method, Silhouette score; Hierarchical clustering (agglomerative, divisive, dendrograms); Density-based clustering (DBSCAN); Dimensionality reduction: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), singular value decomposition (SVD), t-SNE.

units.title: Neural Networks & Model Evaluation
units.topics: Biological vs artificial neurons, Perceptron learning rule; Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), forward propagation, activation functions (ReLU, Sigmoid, Tanh, Softmax); Backpropagation algorithm, chain rule, loss functions; Evaluation metrics: confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC and PR curves, k-fold cross-validation.

objectives: To introduce asymptotic notations and complexity analysis of algorithms.
To implement linear data structures: arrays, linked lists, stacks, and queues.
To master non-linear data structures: trees, binary search trees, AVL trees, and graphs.
To apply classic algorithm design paradigms: divide-and-conquer, greedy, and dynamic programming.

course_outcomes.description: Compute asymptotic time and space complexity using Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notations.
Implement singly, doubly, and circular linked lists, stacks, and queues for real-world problems.
Construct binary trees, BSTs, and self-balancing AVL trees with tree traversals.
Execute graph traversal algorithms (BFS, DFS) and minimum spanning tree algorithms (Prim, Kruskal).
Design dynamic programming and greedy solutions (knapsack, Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall).

units.title: Complexity Analysis & Linear Data Structures
units.topics: Asymptotic notations: O, Omega, Theta; Arrays and matrices; Linked Lists: singly linked lists, doubly linked lists, circular linked lists; Operations: insertion, deletion, searching, traversal.

units.title: Stacks & Queues
units.topics: Stack abstract data type, array and linked list implementation; Applications of stacks: infix to postfix conversion, postfix evaluation, balanced parenthesis; Queue ADT: circular queues, double-ended queues (deque), priority queues.

units.title: Trees & Binary Search Trees
units.topics: Tree terminologies, binary trees, representations, binary tree traversals (inorder, preorder, postorder, level order); Binary Search Trees (BST): insertion, deletion, searching; Balanced search trees: AVL trees, rotations; B-trees and heaps (min-heap, max-heap).

units.title: Graphs & Graph Algorithms
units.topics: Graph representations: adjacency matrix, adjacency list; Graph traversals: Breadth First Search (BFS), Depth First Search (DFS); Topological sort; Minimum Spanning Trees: Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms; Shortest paths: Dijkstra's algorithm.

units.title: Algorithm Design Techniques & Sorting
units.topics: Divide and Conquer: Merge Sort, Quick Sort; Greedy algorithms: Fractional Knapsack, Huffman coding; Dynamic Programming: 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence; Sorting algorithms: Insertion, Selection, Bubble, Radix sort; Hashing: hash tables, collision resolution techniques.

objectives: To teach modern web architectural standards, semantic markup, and responsive stylesheets.
To explore client-side scripting with JavaScript and DOM manipulation.
To build RESTful web services and server-side applications.

course_outcomes.description: Construct standards-compliant, accessible responsive layouts using HTML5 and CSS3.
Write modern ES6+ JavaScript code handling events, asynchronous fetch calls, and DOM modifications.
Develop backend server APIs using Node.js and Express with JSON payload exchanges.
Integrate relational and document databases with backend web application routes.
Implement web security best practices including CORS, CSRF, XSS protection, and JWT authentication.

units.title: HTML5, CSS3 & Responsive Design
units.topics: HTML5 semantic elements, forms, input types, audio and video tags; CSS3 selectors, box model, Flexbox, CSS Grid layout, media queries, mobile-first design principles.

units.title: Client-Side Scripting with JavaScript (ES6+)
units.topics: JavaScript syntax, variables (let, const), data types, functions, arrow functions, template literals, destructuring; DOM manipulation, event listeners; Promises, async/await, Fetch API for AJAX communication.

units.title: Server-Side Programming with Node.js & Express
units.topics: Node.js runtime environment, npm, event loop, modules; Express framework: routing, middleware, request and response objects, error handling, serving static files.

units.title: RESTful API Architecture & Data Persistence
units.topics: REST architectural constraints, HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), status codes, JSON serialization; Database connectivity with MongoDB and MySQL; CRUD operations via ORMs.

units.title: Web Security & Deployment
units.topics: Web security vulnerabilities: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), SQL injection; Authentication & Authorization using JWT and OAuth2; Deployment on cloud platforms, HTTPS, SSL/TLS certificates.

objectives: To introduce software development lifecycles and Agile engineering practices.
To master requirements elicitation, SRS authoring, and architectural design modeling.
To apply software testing methodologies and quality assurance standards.

course_outcomes.description: Select appropriate software process models (Waterfall, Spiral, Agile Scrum) for software projects.
Draft formal Software Requirements Specifications (SRS) based on IEEE 830 guidelines.
Design modular software architectures using UML class, use-case, sequence, and activity diagrams.
Formulate black-box and white-box test cases including boundary value analysis and path coverage.
Apply software maintenance, risk management, and project scheduling techniques (Gantt charts, PERT).

units.title: Software Process Models
units.topics: Nature of software, software engineering layers; Software Process Models: Waterfall, Incremental, Evolutionary, Spiral; Agile development: Agile manifesto, Scrum methodology, sprint planning, user stories, extreme programming (XP).

units.title: Requirements Engineering & Analysis
units.topics: Requirements engineering tasks: inception, elicitation, elaboration, negotiation, specification, validation; Functional and non-functional requirements; Use-case modeling; IEEE 830 standard Software Requirements Specification (SRS) documentation.

units.title: Software Design & UML Modeling
units.topics: Design concepts: abstraction, modularity, architecture, information hiding, functional independence (cohesion and coupling); Object-Oriented design using UML: Class diagrams, Object diagrams, Sequence diagrams, Collaboration diagrams, Activity diagrams, State machine diagrams.

units.title: Software Testing Strategies & Techniques
units.topics: Strategic approach to testing: unit testing, integration testing, validation testing, system testing; Black-box testing: equivalence partitioning, boundary value analysis, cause-effect graphing; White-box testing: basis path testing, cyclomatic complexity, control structure testing; Regression testing.

units.title: Software Project Management & Quality
units.topics: Project metrics, software estimation: COCOMO II model; Project scheduling: Gantt charts, PERT/CPM; Risk management: identification, projection, mitigation; Software Quality Assurance (SQA): ISO 9001, CMMI levels, software maintenance.

objectives: To provide foundations of intelligent agents and heuristic search strategies.
To model knowledge representation and automated reasoning using first-order predicate logic.
To explore planning algorithms and uncertainty management using Bayesian networks.

course_outcomes.description: Formulate state-space search problems for rational agents in complex environments.
Implement informed heuristic search algorithms including A* search and Greedy Best-First Search.
Represent domain knowledge using First-Order Logic (FOL) and apply resolution refutation.
Model probabilistic reasoning in uncertain domains using Bayesian Belief Networks.
Design adversarial game-playing agents using Minimax algorithm with Alpha-Beta pruning.

units.title: Introduction to AI & State-Space Search
units.topics: Definitions of AI, Turing test, intelligent agents, agent architectures, PEAS classification, environment types; Problem formulation as state-space search; Uninformed search strategies: Breadth-First Search (BFS), Depth-First Search (DFS), Uniform-Cost Search (UCS), Iterative Deepening Search (IDS).

units.title: Heuristic Search & Adversarial Games
units.topics: Informed search strategies: Greedy Best-First Search, A* search, admissibility and consistency of heuristics; Local search: Hill climbing, Simulated Annealing, Genetic Algorithms; Adversarial search: Game playing, Minimax algorithm, Alpha-Beta pruning, evaluation functions.

units.title: Knowledge Representation & Logic
units.topics: Knowledge-based agents, propositional logic, inference rules, horn clauses; First-Order Logic (FOL): syntax and semantics, quantifiers, unifications, forward chaining, backward chaining, resolution refutation theorem proving.

units.title: Classical Planning & Constraint Satisfaction
units.topics: Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP): constraint propagation, backtracking search for CSPs, forward checking; Classical planning: PDDL language, STRIPS operators, state-space planning, planning graphs.

units.title: Reasoning under Uncertainty
units.topics: Acting under uncertainty, probability axioms, joint probability distribution, conditional probability, Bayes' rule; Bayesian Belief Networks: semantics, conditional independence; Exact and approximate inference in Bayesian networks.

objectives: To study cloud delivery models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) and deployment architectures.
To examine hypervisor virtualization and container technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).
To analyze cloud storage, distributed file systems, serverless computing, and cloud security.

course_outcomes.description: Differentiate cloud service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) and deployment types (Public, Private, Hybrid).
Analyze CPU, memory, and network virtualization techniques and hypervisors (Type 1 and Type 2).
Deploy containerized microservices using Docker and manage container clusters with Kubernetes.
Examine distributed storage architectures including Google File System (GFS) and Amazon S3.
Implement cloud security, IAM role-based access control, and SLA monitoring.

units.title: Cloud Computing Fundamentals
units.topics: NIST definition of cloud computing, essential characteristics, service models: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), Software as a Service (SaaS); Deployment models: Public, Private, Community, Hybrid; Economics of cloud.

units.title: Virtualization Technology
units.topics: Virtualization concepts, benefits, hardware-assisted virtualization; Hypervisors: Type-1 (bare-metal) and Type-2 (hosted); Virtualization of CPU, memory, and I/O devices; Virtual machine migration (live migration); Comparison between VMs and Containers.

units.title: Containers & Cloud Orchestration
units.topics: Linux namespaces and cgroups; Docker container architecture, Dockerfile, Docker Compose; Container orchestration using Kubernetes: pods, services, deployments, ingress controllers, horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA).

units.title: Cloud Storage & Distributed Computing
units.topics: Distributed file systems: Google File System (GFS), Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS); Cloud object storage (Amazon S3); NoSQL in the cloud; Serverless computing and Function-as-a-Service (AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions).

units.title: Cloud Security, Governance & SLAs
units.topics: Cloud security risks, shared responsibility model, Identity and Access Management (IAM); Encryption at rest and in transit; Service Level Agreements (SLAs), cloud monitoring and auto-scaling, disaster recovery in the cloud.

academic_regulations.attendance_requirement: Students must secure a minimum of 75% aggregate attendance across all registered courses in a semester to be eligible to appear for the End-Semester Examination. A condonation of up to 10% (between 65% and 74%) may be granted on medical grounds subject to approval by the Academic Council.
academic_regulations.grading_system: The institution follows a 10-point Letter Grading Scale: O (Outstanding, 90-100%, Grade Point 10), A+ (Excellent, 80-89%, Grade Point 9), A (Very Good, 70-79%, Grade Point 8), B+ (Good, 60-69%, Grade Point 7), B (Above Average, 55-59%, Grade Point 6), C (Average, 50-54%, Grade Point 5), P (Pass, 40-49%, Grade Point 4), F (Fail, below 40%, Grade Point 0).
academic_regulations.credit_requirements: The total number of credits required for the award of the B.Tech Degree in Computer Science & Engineering (CSE) is 160 credits distributed across 8 semesters.
academic_regulations.examination_pattern: Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) accounts for 40% weightage (2 Mid-Term Tests of 20 marks each, Assignments/Quizzes of 10 marks, normalized to 40). End-Semester Examination accounts for 60% weightage (3-hour comprehensive theory paper). Minimum passing marks are 40% in End-Semester Exam and 40% aggregate.
